questions.title: Who will be the first West Indies bowler to take a five-wicket haul in the opening Test against Pakistan in Tarouba in July 2026?
questions.background: A five-wicket haul means that a bowler takes at least five wickets in a single innings.
questions.resolution_criteria: Source of Truth : Resolve to the first West Indies bowler to reach five wickets in a single innings during the opening Test against Pakistan in Tarouba in July 2026, according to the match scorecard and contemporaneous match reporting. Resolution Date : 2026-07-27 Accepted Answer Format : Answer with the bowler's full name.
questions.current_reasoning: The opening Test at Brian Lara Cricket Academy in Tarouba (July 25-29) will be the venue's maiden Test match, expected to offer seam movement and variable bounce. West Indies' June 16 Test squad for Sri Lanka confirms CWI's managed pace trio of Jayden Seales (Trinidad home bowler and WI's most reliable strike seamer), Shamar Joseph (51 Test wickets at 21.67, returning from shoulder injury), and Alzarri Joseph (returning from back injury), alongside vice-captain and sole specialist spinner Jomel Warrican (19 wickets vs Pakistan in 2025) and veteran Kemar Roach. Conditional on a West Indies bowler claiming a five-for, Seales (29%) and Shamar Joseph (27%) lead as primary new-ball/strike threats, with 10% left for Roston Chase, Anderson Phillip, Justin Greaves, or a recalled Gudakesh Motie.

questions.title: Which candidate will receive the most “encourage” votes in the first UN Security Council straw poll of the 2026 secretary-general selection?
questions.background: António Guterres is serving as UN secretary-general. Informal Security Council straw polls gauge support for potential successors, with members indicating whether they encourage, discourage or have no opinion on each candidate.
questions.resolution_criteria: Source of Truth : Official UN information or contemporaneous reporting by reputable international news organizations describing the first Security Council straw poll in the 2026 secretary-general selection process. Resolution Condition : Resolve to the candidate receiving the highest number of “encourage” votes in that first poll, regardless of subsequent polls or the final appointment. Accepted Answer Format : The candidate’s full name.
questions.current_reasoning: June 25 Korea Times (Jeju Forum) and June 16-24 web reporting (Just Security, PassBlue, The UN Brief) clarify that six active candidates completed mid-June UNGA dialogues ahead of the first UNSC straw poll in the last week of July—including two newly active GRULAC female candidates missed on June 24, Ecuador's María Fernanda Espinosa (former 73rd UNGA President, dialogue June 15) and Guyana's Carolyn Rodrigues-Birkett (UN Ambassador & 2024-25 UNSC member, dialogue June 18), while Mia Mottley is not running. While Rebeca Grynspan retains a narrow edge as the least-polarizing female GRULAC agency head in an approval-style first poll, Rafael Grossi surges to a near dead-heat (0.37 to 0.41) as diplomatic assessments call him a frontrunner with strong P5/crisis-diplomacy stature and high IAEA/Iran salience while four women split the GRULAC female lane. We trim Grynspan (0.45 to 0.42) and Bachelet (0.10 to 0.07, missed Jeju in person), replace non-candidate Mia Mottley with active candidate María Fernanda Espinosa (0.04), hold Macky Sall at 0.03, and leave 0.03 tail mass mainly for Carolyn Rodrigues-Birkett.

questions.title: Who will succeed Brendon McCullum as permanent head coach of England's men's Test team?
questions.background: Brendon McCullum currently coaches England's men's Test cricket team.
questions.resolution_criteria: Source of Truth : An official England and Wales Cricket Board appointment announcement or reliable contemporaneous reporting of that announcement. Resolution : Resolve to the first person formally appointed as McCullum's permanent successor as head coach of England's men's Test team. Interim appointments and appointments solely concerning limited-overs cricket do not count. Resolution occurs when the appointment is announced, even if the coach begins work later. Accepted Answer Format : The appointed coach's full name.
questions.current_reasoning: Major 2026-07-17 update: frontrunner Andy Flower publicly and formally ruled himself out of the England Test head coach race at London Spirit's media day (BBC Sport, Sky Sports, Reuters, ESPNcricinfo, Hindustan Times), confirming he turned down the ECB even with dual-role IPL flexibility because IPL/RCB duties clash with the early English summer. Following Flower's withdrawal, iNews Cricket Correspondent Chris Stocks reports on July 17 that the ECB is now pivoting to former Australia coach Justin Langer as its top target (rated 4/5; strong Ashes rebuilding pedigree and county familiarity, though tempered by LSG IPL ties and past intensity concerns), lifting Langer 0.13 -> 0.26. Newly available Stephen Fleming (co-rated 4/5 by iNews, named by BBC Sport July 17) rises 0.19 -> 0.25 as he just left CSK after 18 years—removing the IPL clash that deterred Flower—was Rob Key's 2022 preference, and publicly welcomed an approach this week. Among remaining shortlisted contenders, Jonathan Trott (0.15 -> 0.16, English, available, named by BBC Sport/iNews 3/5), Richard Dawson (0.07 -> 0.09, English, ECB pathway, named by BBC Sport July 17), and Tom Moody (new entry at 0.07, explicitly named by BBC Sport July 17 alongside Trott, Dawson, and Fleming) round out the top 5, leaving 17% residual for Kumar Sangakkara, Mike Hesson, Adi Birrell, and unlisted options as BBC notes the ECB is still in an initial stage and open to an interim for August's Pakistan series.

questions.title: In which country outside Iran, if any, will US forces strike Iran-aligned armed groups between July 22 and July 29, 2026?
questions.background: Iran-aligned armed groups operate across several Middle Eastern countries, creating potential flashpoints for military confrontation with the United States.
questions.resolution_criteria: Source of Truth : Contemporaneous reporting by Al Jazeera, supported where available by official military statements. Resolution Conditions : Identify the country outside Iran where US forces conduct strikes against Iran-aligned armed groups between July 22 and July 29, 2026, inclusive. Direct US participation in either unilateral or joint strikes qualifies; threats, proposed operations, and diplomatic support do not. Accepted Answer Format : The country's name, or “None” if no qualifying strikes occur.
questions.current_reasoning: Key 2026-07-19/20 updates two days before the July 22-29 strike window shift mass further toward Yemen while trimming Iraq slightly. On Yemen (0.45 -> 0.50): after US forces conducted 9th-10th consecutive nights of strikes on Iran (including electrical/power infrastructure and the Darkhovin construction site) and Brent topped $90 / US gas hit $4/gal, Yemen's Houthis formally broke from sitting out the war today (Al Jazeera, Reuters/Straits Times), declaring an immediate maritime blockade of Saudi Arabia and general mobilization—greatly elevating the risk of Houthi maritime/infrastructure attacks triggering direct US unilateral or joint strikes in Yemen during July 22-29. We cap Yemen at 0.50 rather than higher because no vessel has been struck yet, the blockade is framed against Saudi Arabia (whose Coalition JFC announced Bab al-Mandeb protective measures today), and Qatar/Pakistan are actively pushing a 10-day ceasefire with Iran's Interior Minister in Islamabad today. On Iraq (0.26 -> 0.22): CENTCOM confirmed a third US troop death in northern Iraq on July 18, but it occurred during an accidental controlled detonation of a downed Iranian attack drone—not an Iraqi Shia militia ambush—and Iraqi militias have still abstained from claiming lethal strikes post-PM Al-Zaidi's warm Trump summit, prompting US retaliation exclusively inside Iran so far. None trims only slightly (0.25 -> 0.24, moving ahead of Iraq) because across 10 straight nights of US bombing, zero US strikes have occurred outside Iran and active ceasefire mediation continues. Holding Lebanon 0.02 (President Aoun meets Trump July 21; strikes remain Israeli) and Syria 0.01 (despite IRGC claiming strikes on Al-Tanf, Damascus is anti-Iran and US is reducing presence).

questions.title: Which country will announce a new multinational maritime coalition to protect navigation through the Red Sea, Bab al-Mandeb Strait and Gulf of Aden by August 1, 2026?
questions.background: Attacks on commercial shipping since 2023 have heightened concerns about the security of maritime trade routes through the Red Sea.
questions.resolution_criteria: Source of Truth : Official government announcements or contemporaneous reporting by reputable international news organizations. Resolution Conditions : Identify the country that announces the creation of a new multinational maritime coalition between July 1 and August 1, 2026, inclusive, with a stated purpose of protecting freedom of navigation through the Red Sea, Bab al-Mandeb Strait and Gulf of Aden. Joining an existing coalition does not qualify. Accepted Answer Format : The country's common English name.
questions.current_reasoning: Major 2026-07-20 Red Sea escalation sharply increases Saudi Arabia's lead ahead of the August 1 deadline. Today (Al Jazeera, Reuters/Straits Times, AFP), Yemen's Houthis formally declared a naval/maritime blockade specifically targeting Saudi Arabia, effective immediately, directly endangering the ~4 million bpd of Saudi oil exports diverted to Red Sea port Yanbu (>70% of Saudi exports; 7.4M bpd total transiting Bab al-Mandeb) while Hormuz remains choked off. Crucially, Saudi media (Ajel English, July 20) reported that the Saudi-led Coalition Joint Forces Command (Maj.-Gen. Turki al-Maliki) immediately announced strict operational measures to protect commercial vessels transiting Bab al-Mandeb. While that announcement comes from the existing Yemen coalition rather than creating a brand-new multinational maritime coalition (so it does not itself resolve the question), Riyadh now faces the most urgent existential trigger—alongside its Red Sea Council leadership and July 16 US $1.96bn interoperability arms deal—to unveil a dedicated new Red Sea/Bab al-Mandeb/Gulf of Aden multinational maritime coalition in the next 12 days. Raising Saudi Arabia 0.24 -> 0.34; trimming Egypt 0.17 -> 0.16 (strong #2 given Suez Canal exposure and CTF 153 leadership), United States 0.12 -> 0.11 (already runs Operation Prosperity Guardian and is tied down on Night 10 of bombing Iran), United Kingdom 0.10 -> 0.09, and France 0.09 -> 0.08 (sum 0.78, preserving 22% residual for UAE, India, China, Bahrain, Pakistan, Turkey, Italy, Greece, Djibouti, or others).

questions.title: Which club will sign Bruno Guimaraes from Newcastle United during the 2026 summer transfer window?
questions.background: Bruno Guimaraes joined Newcastle United from Lyon in January 2022 and has established himself as a prominent Premier League midfielder.
questions.resolution_criteria: Source of Truth : An official announcement from Newcastle United or the receiving club confirming a completed permanent transfer during the 2026 summer transfer window. Resolution Conditions : Resolve to the receiving club in the first completed permanent transfer of Guimaraes from Newcastle United during that window. Loan moves, reported interest and unconfirmed agreements do not qualify. Accepted Answer Format : The name of the receiving football club.
questions.current_reasoning: Decisive July 6-16 transfer shift following Brazil's World Cup exit to Norway (July 5) and Newcastle's sales of Anthony Gordon (Barcelona) and Sandro Tonali (Tottenham, £100m): BBC Sport (Sami Mokbel & Ciaran Kelly, July 8) broke that Bruno Guimaraes has formally asked to leave Newcastle as Premier League champions Arsenal accelerate their pursuit; L'Equipe (via Evening Standard, July 14) reported Guimaraes has agreed personal terms with Arsenal on a five-year deal until 2031; and Sports Mole/Sport Witness (July 16) reported Arsenal had a £65m opening bid rejected (preparing a higher €90m bid per Nicolo Schira) while Guimaraes' agency Bertolucci Sports drives talks with Arsenal and offers Newcastle Botafogo's Danilo as a replacement. Meanwhile PlanetFootball (July 8) and Standard (July 14) note Man City (holding Rodri/Kovacic/Anderson) and Man Utd (cold trail, pursuing Tielemans) are not actively bidding. Promoting Arsenal sharply from 0.19 -> 0.55—capped at 0.55 under our unconfirmed-transfer discipline because Newcastle still demand £100m/€120m (a valuation gap that let Spurs hijack Tonali from Arsenal)—with Real Madrid (0.11), Manchester City (0.10, down from 0.24), Barcelona (0.06, cited by TEAMtalk as monitoring), and PSG (0.05) capturing hijack risk alongside 13% residual.
